# How to install the CLI

The `glassfrog` CLI can be installed four ways: the hosted **install script**, **Homebrew**, an **npm** wrapper package, or **from source** with `go install`. Every hosted channel installs the same released binary; pick whichever fits your environment.

> **🚧 Hosted channels need a published release.** The install script (`install.sh`), the Homebrew formula config (`.goreleaser.yaml` `brews`), and the npm wrapper (`npm/`) all exist in the repository, but **no stable release has been published yet** — only a draft `v0.1.0`. Until a stable release is published, the script's download step 404s, the tap has no formula, and the npm package version isn't on the registry, so channels A–C below do not resolve yet. **Install from source meanwhile:**
>
> ```
> go install github.com/Luscii/cli-glassfrog@latest
> ```
>
> This builds `glassfrog` into your Go bin directory (`$(go env GOPATH)/bin`); ensure that directory is on your `PATH`, then skip to [Verify](#verify). The rest of this guide describes the hosted channels as they will work once a stable release is published.

## Choose a channel

| Channel | Best for | Command (once a release is published) |
|---|---|---|
| A. Install script | Any Linux/macOS host, no package manager | `curl -fsSL …/install.sh \| sh` |
| B. Homebrew | macOS/Linux Homebrew users | `brew install luscii/cli-glassfrog/glassfrog` |
| C. npm | Node/JS toolchains, `npx` one-offs | `npm i -g @luscii-healthtech/glassfrog` |
| D. From source | Go developers; works today | `go install github.com/Luscii/cli-glassfrog@latest` |

All four install the same platforms: macOS and Linux on `amd64` or `arm64`. Windows is not supported.

## A. Install script

The one-liner detects your platform, downloads the matching release archive and its checksums file, verifies the archive's integrity, and installs the binary into a per-user directory — no runtime, no package manager, no `sudo`.

### Prerequisites

- A Linux or macOS host on `darwin`/`linux` × `amd64`/`arm64`.
- A downloader (`curl` or `wget`), a checksum utility (`sha256sum`, `shasum -a 256`, or `openssl dgst -sha256`), and `tar`. The script checks for these before downloading and stops with a message if any are missing.

### Steps

Run the one-liner:

```
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Luscii/cli-glassfrog/main/install.sh | sh
```

Or with `wget`:

```
wget -qO- https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Luscii/cli-glassfrog/main/install.sh | sh
```

With no configuration, this installs the latest **stable** release (pre-releases excluded) into `${XDG_BIN_HOME:-$HOME/.local/bin}` and prints the install path and version.

Pin a version or choose a directory with environment variables on the `sh` side of the pipe:

```
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Luscii/cli-glassfrog/main/install.sh | \
  GLASSFROG_VERSION=v1.3.0 GLASSFROG_INSTALL_DIR="$HOME/bin" sh
```

- `GLASSFROG_VERSION` — a tag with or without the leading `v`. A pinned tag installs that exact release, including a pre-release. Unset installs the latest stable release.
- `GLASSFROG_INSTALL_DIR` — the directory to install into; created if absent. It must be writable by your user — the script never escalates privileges.

If the install directory is not on your `$PATH`, the script still succeeds and prints the exact `export PATH=…` line to add (it never edits shell profiles). See the [Install Script reference](../../reference/install-script.md) for the full behaviour.

## B. Homebrew

Homebrew installs the pre-built binary from a dedicated tap — no compilation on your host.

### Steps

Tap and install:

```
brew tap luscii/cli-glassfrog && brew install glassfrog
```

Or in one shot (auto-taps):

```
brew install luscii/cli-glassfrog/glassfrog
```

The tap shorthand `luscii/cli-glassfrog` resolves to `github.com/Luscii/homebrew-cli-glassfrog`; the formula name is `glassfrog` (a formula, not a cask). Homebrew picks the archive for your OS/arch, verifies its sha256 against the formula, and puts `glassfrog` on your `PATH`.

Upgrade to the newest stable release with:

```
brew upgrade glassfrog
```

Homebrew tracks **stable** releases only — a pre-release leaves the tap's formula pointing at the prior stable version.

## C. npm

The npm channel publishes an umbrella package (`@luscii-healthtech/glassfrog`) plus four platform packages. Installing the umbrella pulls in the one matching platform package, whose bundled binary needs no network; the `glassfrog` command is a thin launcher that transparently execs it and propagates its exit code.

### Steps

Install globally:

```
npm i -g @luscii-healthtech/glassfrog
glassfrog <args…>
```

Run a one-off without installing:

```
npx @luscii-healthtech/glassfrog <args…>
```

Pin a version (including a pre-release):

```
npm i -g @luscii-healthtech/glassfrog@1.3.0
```

The installed package version matches the CLI version (`glassfrog --version` reports the same value with the `v` restored). If a platform package can't be resolved at install time, the umbrella's postinstall falls back to downloading and checksum-verifying the release archive; on an unsupported platform (Windows, unsupported arch) it refuses the install with a message naming the supported set and pointing at the script or Homebrew channels.

## D. From source

Requires a Go toolchain. Works today, before any release is published:

```
go install github.com/Luscii/cli-glassfrog@latest
```

This builds `glassfrog` into `$(go env GOPATH)/bin`; ensure that directory is on your `PATH`.

## Verify

Confirm the binary is installed and reports its version:

```
glassfrog version
```

or:

```
glassfrog --version
```

Both report the same value. For a hosted-channel install it equals the resolved release's tag (for example `v1.3.0`); for a `go install` it reflects the built commit. See the [Version Embedding reference](../../reference/version-embedding.md) for what the version reflects across install paths.

## Troubleshooting

**Install script — unsupported platform / missing tooling.** On an unsupported OS or architecture, or with no usable downloader or sha256 utility, the script stops before downloading, names the detected `os`/`arch` (or the missing tool) and the supported set, installs nothing, and exits `2`.

**Install script — checksum mismatch.** If the downloaded archive doesn't match its checksums entry, the script stops before installing, writes no binary, and exits `3`. Re-run — a transient corrupt download usually clears.

**Install script — pinned version not found.** If the requested `GLASSFROG_VERSION` has no published release, the download 404s; the script names the requested version, installs nothing, and exits non-zero.

**Homebrew — checksum mismatch or missing asset.** If the archive's sha256 doesn't match the formula, or the formula references an asset not attached to the release, `brew install` refuses (checksum failure) or fails on the download (404) rather than installing a wrong/partial binary.

**npm — unsupported platform.** On Windows or an unsupported arch, the postinstall refuses with a message naming the detected platform and the supported set, and points you at the install-script or Homebrew channel. Nothing runnable is left behind.

**npm — checksum mismatch or download failure (fallback path).** The postinstall names the integrity or download failure and its next step, places no binary, and fails the `npm install` with a non-zero exit.

**Re-running to upgrade or roll back.** Re-run the install script (or `brew upgrade` / `npm i -g …@latest`) to move to the newest stable release, or pin an older version to roll back. Each run installs the resolved version over the existing binary; there are no partial leftovers.
